text.arabic_uthmani: مِّمَّا خَطِيٓـَٰٔتِهِمْ أُغْرِقُوا۟ فَأُدْخِلُوا۟ نَارًۭا فَلَمْ يَجِدُوا۟ لَهُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَنصَارًۭا

words.gloss_range: fused causal opening, from or because of what follows, making the offenses the source of the punishment sequence
words.prose: {{ar:مِّمَّا}} ({{tr:mimmā}}) launches the ayah from cause rather than spectacle. Its fused, nasal-assimilated form makes the following offenses the source from which the drowning, fire-entry, and failed rescue unfold, while the prepositional source-image is local causality rather than a physical starting place.

topics.headline: causal opening governs the sequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah begins by naming why judgment happens before narrating what happens.
topics.reason: The fused preposition plus relative or masdariyyah element is attached as the causal phrase for the first passive clause, and the following events inherit that launch.

topics.headline: source image becomes moral causality
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the offenses as the point from which the punishment emerges, while local grammar keeps the force causal.
topics.reason: The source value of the preposition survives as image-pressure, but the governed phrase functions here as cause, not physical motion from a place.

topics.headline: fusion and nasal binding make dependency audible
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the opening particle as bound tightly to its content, not as a loose discourse marker.
topics.reason: The written fusion and assimilated nasal support the row's point that the opening phrase is compressed and dependent on what follows.

words.gloss_range: owned plural offenses or culpable errors functioning as the causal ground of judgment
words.root_gloss_range: error, missing the mark, sin, and culpable boundary-crossing; local form selects possessed offenses rather than innocent mistake
words.prose: {{ar:خَطِيٓـَٰٔتِهِمْ}} ({{tr:khaṭīʾātihim}}) makes the cause personal and accumulated: the offenses are theirs, plural, and governed by the causal opening. The hamza gives the plural a caught texture before the passive drowning, and the word turns prior misguidance into owned offenses rather than spectacle. The root's error field remains near the word, but the local possessed plural moves beyond accident into culpable offenses that ground the passive judgment sequence.

topics.headline: possessed offenses supply the cause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees judgment tied to owned offenses, not to an anonymous or unexplained disaster.
topics.reason: The genitive plural noun is governed by the causal opening and carries a third-person plural possessive suffix.

topics.headline: error field is moralized as sin
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the missed-mark field harden into morally accountable offense in this clause.
topics.reason: The broader root includes error and missing the mark, while the local noun and causal frame select culpable offenses; the forgiven-error contrast (2:286) remains a useful boundary.

topics.headline: plural archive and hamza texture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears and sees the offenses as a plural archive rather than a single slip.
topics.reason: The plural noun, suffix, and hamzaed shape support the accumulated-offense payoff without changing the local syntax.

topics.headline: offenses pivot into judgment sequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader follows the movement from prior misguidance and offense into the drowning and fire sequence.
topics.reason: The word sits before the passive verbs and provides the named causal ground for the sequence that follows.

words.gloss_range: completed imposed drowning in passive form, with the group as patients and the agent unnamed
words.root_gloss_range: drowning, sinking, engulfment, and absorption; local Form IV passive selects caused engulfment undergone by the punished group
words.prose: {{ar:أُغْرِقُوا۟}} ({{tr:ughriqū}}) reports the first judgment event as completed passive patienthood. The Form IV passive keeps caused engulfment in view while suppressing the agent, so the group moves from owned offenses into being overwhelmed rather than acting. That passive revoices active divine drowning formulas such as the Pharaoh scene (2:50), and the heavy guttural-to-stop texture hardens the move from petition into enacted judgment.

topics.headline: completed passive drowning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the sinners as patients of a completed judgment event, not as actors in the clause.
topics.reason: The word is a Form IV perfect passive with plural agreement; the passive subject resumes the culpable group and the agent is not named.

topics.headline: caused engulfment and agency loss
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels drowning as engulfment that removes agency, not as a light contact with water.
topics.reason: The root image and Form IV causative shape fit the local passive drowning event.

topics.headline: drowning formula revoiced passively
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can contrast active divine drowning elsewhere (2:50) with this ayah's passive report after cause has been named.
topics.reason: The local passive form supports comparison with active drowning formulas without importing their explicit agent into this clause.

topics.headline: hard sound and report-register shift
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the report harden as the discourse shifts from petition into enacted judgment.
topics.reason: The phonetic observations are local texture and the discourse shift is supported by the ayah's move into narrative judgment.

words.gloss_range: consecutive particle marking the next passive event as tightly sequenced and consequential
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) makes the move from drowning to the next event immediate and consequential. It is not a loose connector; as a split but bound particle before the passive verb, it forms the first audible link in the ayah's chain from cause to punishment to failed recourse.

topics.headline: immediate consequential link
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the next event as following hard on the drowning rather than merely being listed beside it.
topics.reason: The particle links the second passive clause to the first with a strongly licensed sequence relation.

topics.headline: split proclitic exposes the chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can track the ayah's consequence ladder through repeated audible chain markers.
topics.reason: The bundle splits the proclitic particle, and the local syntax shows the linked sequence continuing.

words.gloss_range: imposed passive entry into an explicit fire-domain after drowning
words.root_gloss_range: entering, admission, insertion, and crossing into an inside domain; local Form IV passive selects being made to enter
words.prose: {{ar:أُدْخِلُوا۟}} ({{tr:udkhilū}}) turns the sequence from water-engulfment into fire-enclosure. The passive Form IV makes entry imposed, and the explicit object makes the fire a destination-domain rather than a background image. The same entry root later appears in the household-entry prayer (71:28), so this forced fire-entry becomes the negative pole of entry as refuge.

topics.headline: passive forced entry
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the punished group carried into a new state, not choosing entry or initiating movement.
topics.reason: The verb is a Form IV perfect passive continuing the same plural patients after the first passive.

topics.headline: entry into a named object-domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the entry has a named destination, making the punishment feel like transfer into an enclosed domain.
topics.reason: The passive verb takes an explicit accusative complement, so the inside-boundary image is locally anchored.

topics.headline: entry root reverses into judgment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can contrast this forced entry with the later prayer for household entry in mercy (71:28).
topics.reason: The surah-local return of the entry root supports a valence contrast, while local grammar still selects passive punishment here.

topics.headline: second passive and elemental transfer
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the ayah move from water to fire through matching passive forms, leaving no agency gap for escape.
topics.reason: The second passive follows the first by the particle link and changes the punishment environment from drowning to fire-entry.

words.gloss_range: indefinite accusative fire as the concrete domain entered after drowning
words.root_gloss_range: light, brightness, fire, and burning illumination; local noun selects destructive fire rather than guidance-light
words.prose: {{ar:نَارًۭا}} ({{tr:nāran}}) names the domain into which the passive entry moves them. Its root-nearness to light is felt here as destructive burning, not the surah's light-sign (71:16) or divine-light contrast (24:35), and the indefinite mass noun leaves the entered fire unbounded rather than counted. Its final -an cadence also anticipates the closing denied-helper noun.

topics.headline: fire as object and destination
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees fire as the destination-domain of entry, not only as a punishment label.
topics.reason: The noun is accusative as the explicit complement of the passive entry verb.

topics.headline: light field reversed into fire
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the light-fire field inverted into punitive burning rather than guidance or illumination.
topics.reason: The broader root field includes light, but the local concrete noun and entry construction select fire; the light contrast (24:35) remains a controlled intertextual pressure.

topics.headline: water-to-fire punishment pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that drowning does not end exposure; the sequence reverses from water into fire.
topics.reason: The noun follows the drowning clause through passive entry, producing a local water-to-fire sequence.

topics.headline: indefinite mass noun and cadence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears an unbounded fire-domain that will later rhyme with the final denied helpers.
topics.reason: The singular indefinite accusative form supports mass-domain force and local cadence observations.

words.gloss_range: consecutive particle turning the passive punishment sequence into a negated result clause
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) pivots from what was done to them into what they could not obtain. The second chain marker makes the negated finding clause a consequence of the punishment sequence, not a detached afterthought, and its compact attachment to the negation makes the transition abrupt rather than leisurely.

topics.headline: consequence into negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the failed search for help as the result of the preceding judgment sequence.
topics.reason: The particle links the following negated finding clause to the prior passive entry clause as a consequent clause.

topics.headline: repeated chain marker
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can track all three movements by the repeated particle links.
topics.reason: The local ayah contains repeated consecutive particles before the second passive and before the negated result.

topics.headline: compact marker before negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the transition into negation as compact and abrupt.
topics.reason: The proclitic particle precedes the negation particle and creates the compact result marker noted by the rows.

words.gloss_range: past negation particle governing a jussive imperfect and scoping over the failed finding of helpers
words.prose: {{ar:لَمْ}} ({{tr:lam}}) turns the next imperfect verb into a past negated result: they did not find helpers. It fixes the jussive environment before the helper noun appears, stripping the following verb's final ending and clipping the cadence. The particle's scope reaches the whole finding clause, so the ayah closes not only with punishment but with unavailable recourse.

topics.headline: past negation governs finding
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the failure is grammatically completed as non-finding, not left as future uncertainty.
topics.reason: The particle governs the following jussive imperfect and creates past negation.

topics.headline: negation covers the rescue clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the denial extending across finding, source boundary, and helpers as one closed rescue claim.
topics.reason: The negation governs the finding verb, and the prepositional boundary plus object are attached inside that clause.

topics.headline: compact negation clips the cadence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the clause tighten before the search verb opens.
topics.reason: The particle creates a jussive environment and appears after the chain marker in a compact cadence.

words.gloss_range: negated jussive plural finding, testing whether rescuing support is available to the punished group
words.root_gloss_range: finding, encountering, obtaining, and existence or availability; local clause selects failed finding of available help
words.prose: {{ar:يَجِدُوا۟}} ({{tr:yajidū}}) is the only active verbal form after the passives, but it is active only under negation, with the jussive dropped ending marking failure before the helper object is heard. Its finding field makes rescue a question of availability: the helpers are not merely unseen; they cannot be obtained for the punished group. The non-finding helper formula has a related contrast in denied help for hypocrites (4:145), while here the punished try and fail after drowning and fire.

topics.headline: active finding under negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the only active verb after the passives appears precisely where agency fails.
topics.reason: The verb is a plural jussive imperfect governed by the negation particle, with the same punished group as subject.

topics.headline: finding means obtainable support
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the rescue problem as lack of obtainable aid, not lack of information.
topics.reason: The verb governs an explicit helper object plus beneficiary and exclusion phrases, making availability of aid the local issue.

topics.headline: imperfect after perfect passives
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the ayah shift from completed passive events to a negated active search space.
topics.reason: The imperfect jussive follows two perfect passives and is syntactically active only under negation.

topics.headline: non-finding formula specializes rescue denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can compare another non-finding rescue formula (4:145) while seeing this ayah specialize it after drowning and fire.
topics.reason: The local verb-helper construction supports formula comparison, while the ayah's punishment sequence supplies the local specialization.

words.gloss_range: benefactive or affected-interest preposition attaching the failed finding to the punished group
words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) marks the failed finding as bearing directly on them. As a small split preposition fused to the pronoun in speech, it keeps their affected interest visible inside a compact unit. By placing the beneficiary phrase before the exclusion phrase, the clause foregrounds their vulnerability before it defines the domain from which no help comes.

topics.headline: failed help is for them
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the denied help as their failed benefit or interest, not an abstract absence.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the pronoun as a complement attached to the finding verb.

topics.headline: beneficiary before boundary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader encounters their exposed need before hearing the phrase that excludes alternative help.
topics.reason: The beneficiary phrase precedes the exclusion phrase inside the negated finding clause.

topics.headline: split proclitic keeps relation visible
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can inspect the small preposition that binds the pronoun into the failed search.
topics.reason: The bundle splits the proclitic from the pronoun, making the beneficiary relation explicit for analysis.

words.gloss_range: third-person masculine plural pronoun resuming the punished group as the ones for whom help is unavailable
words.prose: {{ar:هُم}} ({{tr:hum}}) keeps the same group in view at the moment rescue is denied. The pronoun ties the owners of the offenses and the patients of the passives to the exposed beneficiaries of a failed search for help, and its repeated plural-pronoun shape recalls the earlier possessed offenses at the close.

topics.headline: same punished group resumed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks one group through sin, passive punishment, and failed help without losing the referent.
topics.reason: The pronoun refers to the same plural patients and owners already active in the ayah.

topics.headline: denied help lands on them
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the lack of rescue as their own exposed condition, not a general theological statement only.
topics.reason: The pronoun is governed by the beneficiary preposition inside the negated finding clause.

topics.headline: plural pronoun echoes earlier ownership
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the plural pronoun recall the earlier possessive shape as the same group returns at the close.
topics.reason: The pronoun shape matches the earlier plural possessive ending and reinforces referent continuity.

words.gloss_range: preposition opening the excluded source-domain from which no helpers are found
words.prose: {{ar:مِّن}} ({{tr:min}}) opens the final source-domain only to close it. Under negation, it narrows the search for helpers into an exclusion phrase before the indefinite object arrives: no rescue is available from the non-divine side. As the second source-preposition frame, it answers the opening cause-source with a closing excluded rescue-source.

topics.headline: preposition begins excluded domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the clause narrowing from failed finding into a specific excluded source-domain.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the boundary noun in the final exclusion phrase attached to the finding verb.

topics.headline: negation strengthens denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the denied helper class tightened by both negation and source restriction.
topics.reason: The preposition appears inside the negated finding clause before the indefinite helper object.

topics.headline: second prepositional frame mirrors the opening
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can trace an arc from the opening cause-source to the closing excluded rescue-source.
topics.reason: The ayah begins with a fused causal prepositional field and later uses this preposition to open the final exclusion boundary.

words.gloss_range: construct boundary meaning besides or below, defining the non-divine domain from which helpers fail
words.root_gloss_range: nearness, lowness, below-ness, apart-from relation, and inferior rank; local construct selects exclusion relative to the divine name
words.prose: {{ar:دُونِ}} ({{tr:dūni}}) is the boundary word in the rescue denial. It works as a construct tied to the divine name, so the helpers are not denied in a vague place; they are denied in the domain of what is besides and beneath divine authority. The familiar no-patron-or-helper boundary (2:107) is narrowed here to helpers after punishment, and the boundary closes before the final helper noun arrives.

topics.headline: construct boundary governs the exclusion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the helper search fenced by a construct boundary relative to the divine name.
topics.reason: The noun is governed by the preceding preposition and takes the divine name as its genitive complement.

topics.headline: besides and below both shape the domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels non-divine help as both outside the proper source and lower in rank.
topics.reason: The root and formula support overlap between besides-ness and below-ness, while the local construct keeps the force in the exclusion phrase.

topics.headline: besides-God formula meets helper denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can compare the familiar besides-God boundary with no patron or helper (2:107) and see this ayah narrow it to denied helpers after punishment.
topics.reason: The local phrase matches the recurring exclusion formula and is followed by the helper noun.

topics.headline: boundary arrives before helper noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the rescue domain close before the final helper noun arrives.
topics.reason: The exclusion phrase precedes the object that names the denied helpers.

words.gloss_range: genitive proper divine name completing the exclusion boundary and fixing the authority relative to which helpers fail
words.root_gloss_range: deity, worship, devotion, dependence, and awe; local proper name selects the fixed divine referent rather than a generic deity term
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) completes the boundary phrase as a proper, definite reference point. The passives leave the punishing agent unnamed, but the divine name appears where rescue alternatives are closed, making failed help a matter of authority and dependence. Against the earlier plural-gods field (71:23), the singular proper name stands immediately before the final helper denial.

topics.headline: proper name fixes the boundary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the rescue boundary tied to a fixed divine name, not to an abstract higher power.
topics.reason: The proper noun is the genitive complement of the construct boundary and definitizes the phrase.

topics.headline: named authority appears after suppressed agency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that divine authority is named at the rescue boundary, while the mechanics of punishment remain in passive form.
topics.reason: The passive clauses suppress their agent, but the divine name is explicit inside the later exclusion phrase.

topics.headline: deity field becomes dependence boundary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the helper question as a matter of ultimate dependence, while the local form remains the proper name.
topics.reason: The derivational field supplies worship and dependence pressure, but the local word is the proper divine name in a genitive construct.

topics.headline: plural deity field collapses to singular name
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can connect the earlier plural-gods field (71:23) with the singular divine boundary here, where other help is denied.
topics.reason: The surah previously mentions plural claimed gods, and this clause uses the singular proper divine name before denied helpers.

topics.headline: divine name stands before helper denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final helper noun only after divine authority has been named.
topics.reason: The divine name immediately precedes the final helper object across the phrase boundary.

words.gloss_range: indefinite plural helper agents, denied as obtainable rescuers within the non-divine domain
words.root_gloss_range: help, defense, rescue, support, and victory-capacity; local plural agent noun denies effective rescuing agents
words.prose: {{ar:أَنصَارًۭا}} ({{tr:anṣāran}}) closes the ayah on the absent rescue class. Because the noun is plural, indefinite, agentive, and scoped by negation plus the exclusion boundary, the clause denies not sympathy but any effective network of rescuing helpers. The final noun reverses helpers aligned with the divine cause (3:52) and the earlier idol-name echo (71:23), leaving the heard endpoint as unavailable rescue.

topics.headline: helpers denied inside the boundary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees helpers denied specifically within the non-divine domain, not merely absent in general.
topics.reason: The helper noun is the object of the negated finding verb and follows the exclusion phrase.

topics.headline: aid that could change the outcome
topics.reader_payoff: The reader understands the denied help as outcome-changing rescue, not emotional support.
topics.reason: The root field includes help, rescue, defense, and victory; the local active-participial plural selects rescuing agents.

topics.headline: indefinite plural closes the support network
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears not one missing helper but the collapse of the whole possible support network.
topics.reason: The word is an indefinite accusative plural active-participial noun under negation.

topics.headline: helper echoes answer false allegiance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can contrast helpers aligned with Allah (3:52) and the earlier idol-name echo (71:23) with helpers apart from Allah being unavailable here.
topics.reason: The rows give concrete intertexts and surah-local sound/root adjacency; the local clause keeps the contrast under denied rescue.

topics.headline: final word leaves absent rescue
topics.reader_payoff: The reader is left at the ayah's end with the very category of rescue named as unavailable.
topics.reason: The final object completes the negated finding clause after the cause, punishment, and divine boundary have already been stated.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The causal مِمَّا, the passive sequence أُغْرِقُوا فَأُدْخِلُوا, and the failed-rescue clause.
baseline_models.mechanism: Culpable acts initiate a continuous judgment chain: killing by water, compelled entry into kindled fire, then discovery that every substitute source of aid is absent.

activation_trace.role: The culpable-sin branch gives the opening causal phrase its blame-bearing load.
Killing by drowning supplies the first passive transfer and its lethal completion.
Literal ingress makes the second passive a movement across a boundary into a destination.
The kindled-fire branch supplies the destination as an active burning medium.
Finding or encountering turns the final clause into a failed search for actual rescue.
The other-than branch defines the excluded field of substitute powers.
The worshipped-object branch identifies God as the reference against which substitutes fail.
Aid that makes another prevail supplies the concrete rescue the plural actors cannot obtain.

changed_reading.before: The ayah lists drowning, fire, and a lack of helpers.
changed_reading.after: The ayah compresses culpability, two compelled transfers, and the collapse of all substitute aid into one causal judgment process.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The adjoining passives أُغْرِقُوا فَأُدْخِلُوا and the immediate فَلَمْ leave no narrated interval of release.
baseline_models.mechanism: Water first occupies the actors' whole field; ingress then preserves the inside relation while changing its medium to fire. Even what is near remains short of the saving goal, so the sequence has no operative outside.

activation_trace.role: Immersion that takes over an entire field models drowning as total environmental occupation.
Interlaced insides extend the enclosure image from a single threshold to a surrounding condition.
Kindled fire replaces water as the enclosing medium without restoring an exterior.

context_deltas.mechanism: Advance warning opens a period in which the outcome can still be averted; postponement then reaches a fixed limit. The focus ayah's completed passives read as the closure of that timed process, not an unannounced eruption.

context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies offered forgiveness, sent abundant water, rivers, drowning, and rain-as-succor; I infer a reversal from provision to judgment. Alternatively, beneficial rain and lethal flood may be parallel uses of water without an intended inversion.

changed_reading.after: The same material system offered as protected abundance becomes engulfment, and its rescuing capacity is withdrawn.

context_deltas.mechanism: They answer repeated summons by flight and by constructing a garment boundary over themselves. The focus passives reverse that attempted control: they no longer choose what enters their hearing or what encloses them, but are themselves submerged and made to enter.

context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated summons, flight, self-covering, immersion, and forced ingress; I infer a reversal of boundary control. Alternatively, the covering may mark refusal without establishing a spatial counterpart to the focus passives.

changed_reading.after: Their chosen barriers become a failed rehearsal of enclosure: those who controlled access by fleeing and covering are finally enclosed and made to cross a boundary.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context describes a life route from emergence out of earth, through return into it, to a renewed exit. The focus preserves the grammar of directed movement but replaces growth and exit with drowning and ingress into fire, withholding any exit clause.

context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a reversible creation route and a focus route ending in ingress; I infer a counter-cycle in which destination differentiates the actors. Alternatively, the focus may occupy a later phase of the same cycle rather than invert it.

changed_reading.after: The focus reuses creation's movement grammar as a counter-route: emergence and exit give way to submersion and terminal ingress.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earth is made broad and traversable through extended roads and open mountain passes. Drowning then occupies the whole field, erasing its navigable affordances; neither a route nor a helper provides an outside or detour.

context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies broad traversable space followed by total immersion and failed aid; I infer that the flood cancels both physical and social escape routes. Alternatively, the path passage may remain a creation sign without functioning as an escape contrast.

changed_reading.before: They drown and cannot obtain assistance.
changed_reading.after: Drowning is the erasure of a formerly open route-system, and the absent helpers close the last nonspatial route out.

context_deltas.mechanism: Following establishes a chain of dependence, retained gods anchor it cultically, and mass misdirection shows it reproducing socially. The focus plural wrongdoing belongs to that organized system, while the absence of other-than-God helpers exposes the whole network as unable to rescue its members.

structural_cues: 71:21 links following to leaders enlarged by wealth and children but producing loss.

context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies followers, cultic objects, plotting, and propagated misdirection; I infer an organized dependency network whose failure is diagnosed by the focus clause. Alternatively, these may be several wrongs without forming one functional network.

changed_reading.before: Separate sinners discover that no helper is present.
changed_reading.after: A socially reproduced support system reaches judgment and is exposed as structurally incapable of helping anyone within it.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus ayah stands between two repeated increase-prayers over the wrongdoers: first increased misdirection, then increased destruction. Its causal and passive sequence functions as the conversion hinge where accumulated deviation becomes enacted disintegration.

Withholding and confinement from right keep the same wrongdoer class active at the closing escalation.
Destruction, nullification, and breaking supply the terminal state being increased after the focus.
Missing the right course connects accumulated deviation to the focus's causal phrase.
Lethal drowning begins the material enactment of the amplified destructive state.
Ingress into fire carries that enactment forward rather than closing it at drowning.

structural_cues: 71:24 and 71:28 repeat وَلَا تَزِدِ الظَّالِمِينَ إِلَّا with different terminal nouns.

context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a repeated frame, changed complements, and the intervening judgment sequence; I infer that 71:25 converts compounding deviation into compounding destruction. Alternatively, the two prayers may merely flank the report without making it a transformation operator.

changed_reading.before: The focus reports punishment caused by past sins.
changed_reading.after: The focus is the active hinge where an accumulating regime of misdirection crosses into an accumulating regime of destruction.

context_deltas.mechanism: The same ingress root governs two sharply different destination-relations: compelled entry into fire in the focus and voluntary entry into Noah's house as a believer under a prayer for forgiveness. Entry becomes a sorting operation whose destination discloses security or exposure.

structural_cues: 71:25 uses passive plural ingress into fire; 71:28 uses singular active ingress into my house.
The later entrant is immediately qualified by believing language and included in a forgiveness prayer.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated ingress with opposed destinations, agency, security, and prayer; I infer a destination-based sorting contrast. Alternatively, the house phrase may only delimit the prayer's recipients and not formally oppose the fire-entry.

changed_reading.before: Entry into fire is merely the second punishment.
changed_reading.after: Ingress is a sorting grammar: compelled entry leads into consuming exposure, while believing entry leads into shelter, security, and requested covering.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the rain-missed-land branch is not the surface sense of خَطِيئَاتِهِمْ. It remains anchored through the packet's focus branch, abundant-rain context, and literal drowning; downstream prose should render it only as a branch-image reversal, never as a replacement translation of wrongdoing.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The juxtaposition of خَطِيئَاتِهِمْ and أُغْرِقُوا within the same causal clause.

changed_reading.after: As a contained branch image, what could miss the proper target or be missed by beneficial rain is answered by destructive water that does not miss its recipients.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is form-distant because it uses the packet's non-dominant ج د د mapping for وَجَدُوا and its shoreline branch. It remains valid as an activation because the focus itself joins failed finding to drowning and absent aid; downstream prose must call it a spatial resonance, not a lexical gloss of يَجِدُوا.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: أُغْرِقُوا ... فَلَمْ يَجِدُوا ... أَنصَارًا joins drowning directly to failed finding and rescue.

The non-dominant shoreline branch spatializes failed finding as the absence of a reachable edge.
Nearness short of the goal makes a seemingly close edge remain unreachable.
Concrete aid converts the unreachable shoreline into an image of rescue failure.

changed_reading.before: They fail to locate anyone who can help.
changed_reading.after: As an exploratory spatial resonance, the drowned actors find no shore of rescue: every near edge falls short and no aid can bring them out.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because shared root inventory does not make cosmic light and punitive fire semantically interchangeable. It remains anchored in the exact ن و ر occurrences and their distinct branches; downstream prose should present hostile or inverted luminosity as symbolic activation, not etymological identity.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: فَأُدْخِلُوا نَارًا makes entry terminate in the fire branch of ن و ر.

activation_trace.role: Illumination supplies the ordered cosmic light against which the focus fire is contrasted.
Kindled fire activates a consuming rather than orienting form within the same root inventory.
Ingress makes the changed luminosity a destination they enter rather than a sign they observe.

changed_reading.before: Fire is only a burning destination.
changed_reading.after: As a contained branch activation, they enter an inverted luminosity: cosmic light that could orient is answered by fire that exposes and consumes.

strongest_changes: The focus sequence closes a long warning-and-deferral process at its fixed deadline.
Life-giving rain and rivers reverse into drowning, while rain's succoring function becomes unavailable.
The ayah acts as a hinge between increased misdirection in 71:24 and increased destruction in 71:28.
Repeated ingress distinguishes compelled entry into fire from believing entry into a sheltered house.
Follower, deity, and misdirection relations turn the missing helpers into the collapse of an organized support network.
summary.what_was_special: The packet repeatedly changed the focus from a flat punishment report into a set of directional reversals: warning to closure, provision to engulfment, self-covering to imposed enclosure, exit to ingress, open routes to route erasure, and cultic support to disclosed incapacity. The split وَجَدَ mapping also preserved a contained no-shore image that a conservative reading would likely lose.
remaining_uncertainties: The passive sequence may mark immediate temporal succession, rhetorical compression, or both.
The counter-cycle and dual-ingress models depend on reading nearby directional parallels as deliberate contrasts rather than simple sequence.
The rain-miss, shoreline, and inverted-luminosity activations should remain explicitly exploratory and should not replace surface lexical senses.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Wrong direction culminates in water without traversable direction.** **خ ط ء B002** supplies culpable wrongdoing and **B001** missing the right direction; **غ ر ق B001–B002** supplies drowning and killing by drowning. Earlier 71:20 offered broad paths, while 71:24 described losing the path. The packet supplies that spatial sequence; the abductive arrow is that accumulated misdirection ends in a medium where their prepared terrestrial routes no longer function. The ayah reads drowning as the material closure of path-loss.

2. **Rain missed morally returns as saturation physically.** **خ ط ء B003** supplies land missed by rain while its surroundings receive it, and **غ ر ق B003** supplies land saturated with water. The surah earlier offered abundant rain and gardens in 71:11–12. The packet supplies missed rain, promised rain, and saturation; the inferred reversal is that refusal misses water as beneficent cultivation and meets it as excess. This is a strong latent water reading without replacing culpable sin through **خ ط ء B002**.

3. **Light becomes fire after refused illumination.** *Nāran* is assigned by the packet to **ن و ر B002**, burning fire, while 71:16 used **ن و ر B001** for the moon’s light and **س ر ج B001** for the solar lamp. The passive sequence moves directly from immersion in water to caused entry into fire. The packet supplies both luminous branches; the abductive arrow is that signs rejected as illumination return as burning exposure. The ayah makes judgment a reversal of the earlier cosmic light-system.

4. **All substitute means fail at the point of entry.** **د خ ل B001** supplies caused entry, **و ج د B001** finding and **B003** capacity or means, **د و ن B003** what is other than or below, and **ن ص ر B001** aid that makes one prevail. The negated finding construction removes both helpers and practical means outside God. The packet supplies inability and absent aid; the abductive arrow is that preserved deities and social abundance had functioned as imagined means until the forced transition exposed their nonexistence as support.

5. **Rain-help is absent even inside the water-domain.** **ن ص ر B004** supplies helping rain and **B007** tributary watercourses. Those branches are activated by the surrounding rain, rivers, and drowning. The inferred irony is that the water system once offered as aid cannot itself become an independent helper against divine judgment. “No helpers” therefore closes the hydrological mechanism as well as the social one.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 71:28 supplied the surprising counter-entry: a believer enters a house characterized by shelter and trust, opposing caused entry into fire. Its forgiveness-prayer also showed that protective mediation still exists, but only through God rather than helpers “besides” God.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Culpable errors as accumulated directional misses.** **Lexical evidence:** `خ ط ء B002` is culpable sin, while dormant `خ ط ء B001` is missing or passing beyond what is right; `ض ل ل B001` at 71:24 supplies deviation from aim. **Structural cue:** the causal opening follows the route, following, and misguidance sequence of 71:20-24. **Assigned role:** each culpable act is a miss that accumulates along a misdirected course. **Abductive move:** I infer aggregation from the plural and the preceding route mechanism. **Reading change:** `خطيئاتهم` reads as enacted directional failures, not a disconnected ledger.

2. **From chosen motion to compelled transport.** **Lexical evidence:** `غ ر ق B001` is drowning in water, `د خ ل B001` is entering or causing entry, and `ن و ر B002` is burning fire. **Structural cue:** two passive verbs compress immersion and then entry, reversing from water to fire after active following and plotting. **Assigned role:** consequence takes control of bodies once chosen direction reaches its end. **Abductive move:** I infer loss of agency from passive form and sequence; the packet supplies the elemental reversal. **Reading change:** the verse is a transfer from self-directed following to imposed movement across incompatible media.

3. **Failed help as empirical discovery.** **Lexical evidence:** `و ج د B001` is finding or coming upon a sought thing; `ن ص ر B001` is aid that produces prevailing; `د و ن B003` is other than or below. **Structural cue:** retained worshipped objects at 71:23 are followed by a crisis in which no helpers are found besides Allah. **Assigned role:** crisis tests whether the preserved objects can instantiate aid. **Abductive move:** I infer a failed search from `لم يجدوا`, not merely abstract nonexistence. **Reading change:** the absence of helpers becomes an experienced falsification of misplaced reliance.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The reproduction explanation at 71:26-27 showed why consequence is followed by a request to terminate the maintenance chain, while the trusting household at 71:28 supplied its positive alternative. The failed search for helpers therefore became both falsification of old reliance and prelude to correctly located shelter.

baseline.text: Günahları yüzünden boğuldular, ardından ateşe sokuldular; Allah'tan başka kendilerine yardımcılar bulamadılar.

findings.text: Günahların doğru yönü ıskalama çağrışımı, önceki yollar ve sapma dizisi içinde her suçu yanlış rotada biriken somut bir yön hatası haline getirir.
Kendi seçtikleri izleme hareketinden sonra edilgen biçimde boğulup ateşe sokulmaları, bedenlerin yönünü artık sonucun belirlediği bir yetki kaybını gösterir.
Yağmurun uğramadığı toprak ile suya doymuş toprak çağrışımları, yararlı yağmuru kaçıranların aynı su alanıyla taşkın fazlalık olarak karşılaşmasını görünür kılar.
Ayın aydınlığı ile buradaki ateşin ortak kökü, yol gösterici ışığın reddedilişten sonra yakıcı bir açığa çıkışa dönüşmesini gösterir.
Yardımcıları 'bulamamaları', korudukları ilahların kriz anında gerçekten destek üretip üretemediğini sınayan ve yanlış güveni deneyimle çürüten başarısız bir arayıştır.
Yardım kökündeki yardım eden yağmur ve yan su yolu çağrışımları, daha önce nimet olan su düzeninin Allah'tan bağımsız bir kurtarıcıya dönüşemeyeceği ironisini ekler.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 71:15-28] Light Can Guide Sight or Capture It
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Visibility is an active relation: light may reveal an orienting sign, overwhelm perception, or manufacture a persuasive appearance.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The same optical field contains landmark, glare, nocturnal hunter, cosmetic enhancement, false lamp, and consuming fire.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Illumination makes landmarks and routes legible
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Light reveals forms and elevated markers by which an observer can orient thought and movement.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: direct visual apprehension (`quranic:root_000531:B001/m01`); reflective judgment and deliberation (`quranic:root_000531:B002/m01`); reciprocal visibility between facing sides (`quranic:root_000531:B004/m01`); visible aspect and mirror (`quranic:root_000531:B006/m01`); raised banner (`quranic:root_000531:B011/m01`); showing a thing to another (`quranic:root_000531:B012/m01`); interrogative summons to notice (`quranic:root_000531:B013/m01`); luminous moon (`quranic:root_001255:B001/m01`); illumination (`quranic:root_001564:B001/m01`); visible beacon or boundary marker (`quranic:root_001564:B005/m01`); luminous lamp (`quranic:root_000693:B001/m01`); sun and daylight (`quranic:root_000818:B001/m01`); two celestial stars named as vultures (`quranic:root_001496:B006/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Vision, reflection, mirror, banner, beacon, moon, sun, and lamp occupy one orienting scene. Light makes a sign available; a sign gives sight a target; and sight becomes deliberative rather than merely sensory. Celestial luminosity thus supports both wayfinding and recognition.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 71:15-28] Light Can Guide Sight or Capture It
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Visibility is an active relation: light may reveal an orienting sign, overwhelm perception, or manufacture a persuasive appearance.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The same optical field contains landmark, glare, nocturnal hunter, cosmetic enhancement, false lamp, and consuming fire.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Glare and nocturnal exposure turn the observer into prey
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Excess or badly situated light confuses sight, prevents rest, and exposes a subject to hunters or hostile force.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: hunting by moonlight (`quranic:root_001255:B003/m01`); sight bewildered by intense whiteness (`quranic:root_001255:B005/m01`); wakefulness under moonlight (`quranic:root_001255:B009/m01`); property left unguarded at night (`quranic:root_001255:B011/m01`); refractory animal or hostile disposition (`quranic:root_000818:B002/m01`); open hostility (`quranic:root_000818:B003/m01`); withholding what lies behind one's back (`quranic:root_000818:B006/m01`); flight and instability (`quranic:root_001564:B006/m01`); enmity between groups (`quranic:root_001564:B007/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Light no longer simply serves the viewer. It blinds, keeps the subject awake, exposes unattended property, and gives the night hunter an advantage. The optical relation reverses: what should reveal the path can make the observer visible to a hostile gaze.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 71:15-28] Light Can Guide Sight or Capture It
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Visibility is an active relation: light may reveal an orienting sign, overwhelm perception, or manufacture a persuasive appearance.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The same optical field contains landmark, glare, nocturnal hunter, cosmetic enhancement, false lamp, and consuming fire.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Manufactured brilliance can pass for truth
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Surface enhancement, display, and false luminosity create an attractive but unreliable appearance.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: beautifying and brightening a face or object (`quranic:root_000693:B003/m01`); false lamp and lying speech (`quranic:root_000693:B005/m01`); gambling victory by deception (`quranic:root_001255:B007/m01`); action performed to be seen (`quranic:root_000531:B005/m01`); cosmetic coating (`quranic:root_001564:B009/m01`); smoke pigment used as kohl or tattoo (`quranic:root_001564:B008/m01`); ochre coating (`quranic:root_001438:B004/m01`); fabricated speech (`quranic:root_000434:B007/m01`); fire and branding flame (`quranic:root_001564:B002/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Cosmetic brightness and ostentatious display can simulate disclosure while hiding fabrication. The false lamp joins verbal invention to optical persuasion, and the same fire that lends brilliance can brand or consume. This gives the polemic a precise pressure point: appearance is not self-authenticating.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 71:15-28] Human Life Is Planted, Returned, and Raised
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Human existence follows a cultivated cycle of placement in earth, growth, return, and renewed emergence.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Agriculture, burial, education, and biological descent become phases of one generative process.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: The earth is a growing medium for human formation
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A cultivator places living material in receptive ground, tends it, and brings a formed human subject to maturity.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: soft fertile earth (`quranic:root_000025:B002/m01`); plant emerging from ground (`quranic:root_001465:B001/m01`); deliberate planting (`quranic:root_001465:B002/m01`); source and growing site (`quranic:root_001465:B005/m01`); human growth and upbringing (`quranic:root_001465:B006/m01`); grain spike extending from the stalk (`quranic:root_000672:B008/m01`); tree flower as emitted light (`quranic:root_001564:B004/m01`); seed covered by soil (`quranic:root_001307:B008/m01`); fruit enclosed in its sheath (`quranic:root_001307:B010/m01`); origination (`quranic:root_000434:B002/m01`); gradual repair and completion (`quranic:root_000532:B002/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Earth supplies setting and material receptivity; planting supplies agency; seed-covering supplies protected latency; and upbringing extends cultivation into human care. “Growing you” therefore remains biologically, pedagogically, and spiritually active.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 71:15-28] Human Life Is Planted, Returned, and Raised
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Human existence follows a cultivated cycle of placement in earth, growth, return, and renewed emergence.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Agriculture, burial, education, and biological descent become phases of one generative process.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Burial is a return to the source before emergence
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A subject re-enters its originating ground, disappears within a terminal dwelling, and is brought outward again.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: return after departure (`quranic:root_001058:B001/m01`); place and time of return (`quranic:root_001058:B002/m01`); repeated visitation of the sick or mourning place (`quranic:root_001058:B005/m01`); benefit that returns to its recipient (`quranic:root_001058:B006/m01`); ancient return-road (`quranic:root_001058:B009/m01`); entering a place or state (`quranic:root_000464:B001/m01`); penetration to the outside (`quranic:root_000400:B001/m01`); extraction from concealment (`quranic:root_000400:B002/m01`); grave as a house (`quranic:root_000166:B007/m01`); remote village or grave (`quranic:root_001307:B012/m01`); disappearance into earth (`quranic:root_000913:B002/m01`); clinging to the ground (`quranic:root_000025:B006/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Return, entry, disappearance, grave-house, extraction, and exit form one reversible spatial sequence. Earth is not merely the place of disposal; it is the prior source and temporary interior from which renewed outward movement is possible.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 71:15-28] Prepared Ground Becomes Route, Dwelling, and Contested Residence
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Space is made usable by spreading, opening, traversing, and inhabiting it; judgment then contests who may remain and who may enter a protected house.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The earth-carpet is not passive scenery but civic infrastructure whose routes lead either to inhabited refuge or to an emptied settlement.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: House, household, and resident define protected belonging
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A dwelling shelters a recognized household and admits a trusted entrant into its interior.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: shelter and dwelling (`quranic:root_000166:B001/m01`); household and dependents (`quranic:root_000166:B002/m01`); house of inherited standing (`quranic:root_000166:B008/m01`); entry into an interior (`quranic:root_000464:B001/m01`); inward confidential domain (`quranic:root_000464:B003/m01`); outsider incorporated among a people (`quranic:root_000464:B005/m01`); settled householder or resident (`quranic:root_000499:B007/m01`); security and trustworthy belonging (`quranic:root_000054:B001/m01`); faith as heart-settling assent (`quranic:root_000054:B002/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Belonging is built through shelter, kin relation, recognized standing, admission, and trust. Entry is not generic movement; it crosses a social boundary into an interior whose members are secured by a shared assent.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 71:15-28] The Plot Is Cultivated Beneath a Treated Surface
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A destructive plan develops through hidden preparation, managed inputs, and a surface that conceals the condition of what is ripening underneath.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Plotting becomes an agricultural and cosmetic operation: water the hard ground, grow the plant, coat the exterior, and discover rot in the fruit.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Concealed defect is covered by a persuasive finish
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: An internal fault is held beneath an applied surface that improves appearance while obscuring what lies inside.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: inward corruption, deceit, and hostility (`quranic:root_000464:B004/m01`); concealed interior and confidence (`quranic:root_000464:B003/m01`); interpenetrating internal parts (`quranic:root_000464:B008/m01`); planning and arranging by night (`quranic:root_000166:B004/m01`); chief share of a great affair (`quranic:root_001281:B002/m01`); ochre coating (`quranic:root_001438:B004/m01`); cosmetic plaster or depilatory coating (`quranic:root_001564:B009/m01`); covering and concealment (`quranic:root_001307:B001/m01`); denial that hides truth (`quranic:root_001307:B003/m01`); visible appearance or mirror (`quranic:root_000531:B006/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The scene distinguishes substrate from finish. Corruption and hostility occupy the inward layer; ochre, cosmetic coating, and general covering occupy the visible layer. The plot's danger lies in the functional gap between those layers.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 71:15-28] Covering Divides Denial, Burial, and Mercy
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Covering changes what remains available to sight, memory, consequence, or protection; its moral force depends on what is covered and for what end.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Seed-cover, truth-cover, grave, flood, expiation, and forgiveness are materially similar operations with opposed outcomes.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Engulfment hides body, route, and memory
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Water, earth, or darkness occupies the subject's whole field until location, route, and retained trace disappear.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: sinking under water to destruction (`quranic:root_001080:B001/m01`); total occupation of a field (`quranic:root_001080:B005/m01`); ground filled with water (`quranic:root_001080:B003/m01`); disappearance and burial (`quranic:root_000913:B002/m01`); loss of location (`quranic:root_000913:B003/m01`); loss from memory (`quranic:root_000913:B004/m01`); remote grave or settlement (`quranic:root_001307:B012/m01`); lower realm beneath another (`quranic:root_000502:B001/m01`); entering an enclosing state (`quranic:root_000464:B001/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 71:18 (`خ ر ج` as the counter-operation); 71:24 and 71:27 (`ض ل ل`); 71:25 (`غ ر ق`, `د خ ل`, `د و ن`); 71:26-27 (`ك ف ر`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Immersion does more than kill. It removes coordinates, interrupts the route, suppresses the trace, and turns the surrounding medium into a total cover. The later promise of exit from earth stands as the exact counter-operation to this disappearance.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 71:15-28] Covering Divides Denial, Burial, and Mercy
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Covering changes what remains available to sight, memory, consequence, or protection; its moral force depends on what is covered and for what end.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Seed-cover, truth-cover, grave, flood, expiation, and forgiveness are materially similar operations with opposed outcomes.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Mercy covers fault while preserving the person
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A fault is covered in a way that removes its punitive effect without erasing the subject, who is instead admitted into security.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: preserving cover (`quranic:root_001096:B001/m01`); forgiveness shielding from sin's effect (`quranic:root_001096:B002/m01`); expiation that covers an offense (`quranic:root_001307:B009/m01`); security and trust (`quranic:root_000054:B001/m01`); assent that settles the heart (`quranic:root_000054:B002/m01`); prayer for response (`quranic:root_000054:B003/m01`); entering an interior (`quranic:root_000464:B001/m01`); dwelling as refuge (`quranic:root_000166:B001/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Merciful covering preserves identity and relationship. Expiation removes the offense's operative trace, trust settles the entrant, and the house receives rather than obliterates the person. This is the opposite of engulfment: the fault disappears while the subject remains locatable and sheltered.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 71:15-28] Judgment Closes Every Exit and Settles the Account
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Terminal judgment occupies the subject's environment, removes assistance and alternatives, and converts accumulated wrong into irreversible loss.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Water, fire, accounting, broken material, failed search, and denied redress converge on one terminal condition.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Immersion and fire form consecutive enclosures
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Water first closes the outer field by engulfment; entry then transfers the subject into a second enclosing medium of fire.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: drowning and submersion (`quranic:root_001080:B001/m01`); killing by drowning (`quranic:root_001080:B002/m01`); total occupation and engulfment (`quranic:root_001080:B005/m01`); decorated bridle wholly covered by its material (`quranic:root_001080:B008/m01`); entry into an interior (`quranic:root_000464:B001/m01`); fire and consuming flame (`quranic:root_001564:B002/m01`); lower or nearer enclosing realm (`quranic:root_000502:B001/m01`); no alternative besides the enclosing thing (`quranic:root_000502:B003/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The sequence is spatially exact. Drowning fills the first medium until no external field remains; entry then crosses into fire, a second total environment. The fully overlaid bridle provides a shape analogy for engulfment: nothing of the underlying object escapes the covering material.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 71:15-28] Judgment Closes Every Exit and Settles the Account
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Terminal judgment occupies the subject's environment, removes assistance and alternatives, and converts accumulated wrong into irreversible loss.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Water, fire, accounting, broken material, failed search, and denied redress converge on one terminal condition.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Search finds neither capacity nor helper
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A distressed subject searches for an available resource, ally, or alternative but encounters absence at every role.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: finding and reaching a sought thing (`quranic:root_001626:B001/m01`); material capacity and means (`quranic:root_001626:B003/m01`); grief and distressed attachment (`quranic:root_001626:B004/m01`); anger and grievance (`quranic:root_001626:B005/m01`); aid that overcomes an enemy (`quranic:root_001510:B001/m01`); self-redress after oppression (`quranic:root_001510:B002/m01`); rescuing rain and relief (`quranic:root_001510:B004/m01`); aid as a granted good (`quranic:root_001510:B005/m01`); tributary carrying water from afar (`quranic:root_001510:B007/m01`); alternate or substitute (`quranic:root_000502:B003/m01`); low or inadequate thing (`quranic:root_000502:B002/m01`); security and reliable trust (`quranic:root_000054:B001/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Finding requires a target, capacity requires usable means, and aid requires another agent. Judgment removes all three. Emotion remains, but it cannot become resource, substitute, or redress. The contrast with secure believers makes the absence relational as well as material.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 71:15-28] Judgment Closes Every Exit and Settles the Account
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Terminal judgment occupies the subject's environment, removes assistance and alternatives, and converts accumulated wrong into irreversible loss.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Water, fire, accounting, broken material, failed search, and denied redress converge on one terminal condition.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Wrong resolves into deficit, breakage, and dust
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Misplaced action accumulates as a deficient account and ends in the physical breakup of what had seemed valuable or durable.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: general diminution (`quranic:root_000409:B001/m01`); lost commercial capital (`quranic:root_000409:B002/m01`); deficient measure (`quranic:root_000409:B003/m01`); revenue paid out (`quranic:root_000400:B003/m01`); partners or heirs dividing shares (`quranic:root_000400:B012/m01`); written register or ledger (`quranic:root_000502:B005/m01`); missing the right direction (`quranic:root_000420:B001/m01`); deliberate offense (`quranic:root_000420:B002/m01`); grievance seeking redress (`quranic:root_000967:B003/m01`); putting a thing in the wrong place or time (`quranic:root_000967:B004/m01`); withholding a right (`quranic:root_000967:B008/m01`); destruction and fragmentation (`quranic:root_000174:B001/m01`); precious material reduced to unworked fragments (`quranic:root_000174:B002/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Wrong is first a directional error, then a misplacement or withheld right, then a measurable deficit. Destruction finally translates the account into matter: fashioned value is broken back into fragments. The terminal loss is both juridical and material.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 71:15-28] Household Continuity Forks Into Corrupt and Believing Succession
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A household transmits identity through birth, upbringing, following, and admission; the transmitted direction can reproduce rebellion or secure trust.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Lineage is a transmission system rather than a guarantee: biological generation, fostered formation, social imitation, and house-entry can carry opposed inheritances.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Faith admits kin and community into a protected house
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Trusted entrants cross into a dwelling where kinship and shared assent define a secure community.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: dwelling and refuge (`quranic:root_000166:B001/m01`); household and dependents (`quranic:root_000166:B002/m01`); inherited household standing (`quranic:root_000166:B008/m01`); entry into an interior (`quranic:root_000464:B001/m01`); security and trust (`quranic:root_000054:B001/m01`); faith as settled assent (`quranic:root_000054:B002/m01`); prayer seeking response (`quranic:root_000054:B003/m01`); parents (`quranic:root_001683:B002/m01`); child or descendant (`quranic:root_001683:B001/m01`); forgiveness preserving the entrant (`quranic:root_001096:B002/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: House-entry integrates spatial, familial, and confessional belonging. Trust qualifies the entrant, forgiveness preserves rather than excludes, and kinship is widened to believing men and women. This is a deliberately formed succession opposed to the lineage of 71:27.

concept_map.definition: Suda batıp suyun altında kalarak boğulmak veya bir başkasını bu duruma düşürmektir. Borç, bela ya da nimet tarafından bütünüyle kuşatılma buna benzetilir; özel bir söz öbeği de kurtuluş ümidi kalmayan kişinin yakarışını anlatır.

facets.statement: Bir kişinin suda batması, su altında kalması ve bunun sonucunda boğulmasıdır.
Bir başkasını su içinde bırakarak boğulmasına yol açan ettirgen kullanım da dalın içindedir.
Borç, bela veya nimet içinde çıkışsız kalma, suyun altında kalmaya benzetilen bir kapsam genişlemesidir.
Boğulmak üzere olanın yakarışı, yalnızca belirli bir söz öbeğinde çaresizce yardım dileme anlamı taşır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar suda batıp boğulmayı ortak çekirdek olarak verir; başkasını boğma ettirgen kullanımdır. Borç, bela ve nimet altında kalma fiziksel boğulmaya benzetilir, özel yakarış sözü ise ancak son çare olarak yardım dilemeyi anlatır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi öldürmeyi ortak sonuç olarak verir, fakat yenidoğana ilişkin anlatımlar mekanizmayı aynı biçimde sunmaz: bazıları su içinde boğmayı, biri ise doğum sıvısının bebeğin burnuna kaçmasına yol açan özensizliği anlatır. Bu nedenle dal korunabilir, ancak her örneği kasıtlı olarak suya batırma diye okumamak gerekir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Özgül yenidoğan anlatısında sıvı yoluyla ölüme neden olma vardır; bunun ardından sözcük bütün öldürmeler için genişletilmiş olabilir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, öldürme bildiren biçimi yenidoğanla ilgili kalıpla birlikte verir; yenidoğan örneğinin ayrıntıları genel öldürme anlamına taşınmaz.

concept_map.definition: Birini sıvı içinde boğarak ya da sıvının solunum yoluna girmesine neden olarak öldürmektir. Yenidoğana ilişkin özgül anlatımdan hareketle aynı adlandırma daha sonra öldürmenin geneline de yayılmıştır.

facets.statement: Bir insanın sıvıyla bağlantılı bir boğulma süreci sonucunda öldürülmesidir.
Özgül anlatıda ebe, yenidoğanı su içinde tutar veya doğum sıvısının burnuna girmesine yol açarak ölümüne neden olur.
Sıvıyla boğma anlamından hareketle söz, araç belirtilmeden genel olarak öldürme için de kullanılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak sonucu öldürmedir. Yenidoğan örneği kimi anlatımda su içinde boğma, kimi anlatımda doğum sıvısının burna girmesine yol açma biçimindedir; bu özgül kullanımdan genel öldürme anlamına geçildiği de belirtilir.

neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal suyu toprağa gönderme ve toprağı sulayarak iyi duruma getirme eylemini sözlükselleştirir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da suyun toprağa yayılması ve toprağı kaplaması sahnesini paylaşır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu dal su verme işlemini, odak dalıysa bu işlemin sonunda oluşan en ileri doygunluk durumunu öne çıkarır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi yayı veya oku çekişin ulaşabileceği son sınıra kadar götürmeyi ortak biçimde anlatır. Bir anlatım çekişin ok üzerindeki belirli bölüme kadar sürmesini ayrıntılandırır; bu ayrıntı, genel çekme ya da ok atma değil, yay çekişinin tamamlanma derecesidir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Anlam yalnızca okçuluk yapısında yayın son sınırına kadar çekilmesidir; genel çekme, yayın denenmesi veya okun fırlatılması değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalnızca yay çekme yapısına bağlıdır ve bu yapının son sınıra ulaşma koşulunu yalın kök anlamı gibi genelleştirmez.

concept_map.definition: Ok atmaya hazırlanırken yayı veya oku, yayın izin verdiği son çekiş sınırına kadar güçlü biçimde çekmektir. Belirleyici olan çekme eylemi değil, çekişin bütünüyle tamamlanmasıdır.

facets.statement: Yayı, çekilebileceği son sınıra kadar germek ve çekiş payının tamamını kullanmaktır.
Ok üzerindeki bağlama bölümünün yaya yaklaşmasına kadar süren şiddetli çekiş, işlemin teknik sınırını açıklar.
Yayı son sınırına kadar çekme görüntüsü, aşırılık ve ölçüyü kaçırma için atasözü niteliğinde de kullanılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar okçunun yayı veya oku son çekiş noktasına kadar götürmesinde birleşir. Teknik ayrıntı, çekişin ok üzerindeki bağlama bölümüne kadar sürerek yayın bütün çekme payını tüketmesidir. Bu çekiş görüntüsü, aşırılık ve ölçüyü kaçırma için atasözü niteliğinde de kullanılır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Yalnızca okçulukta, yayın çekiş payının bütünüyle kullanıldığı söz öbeğini karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Yay bağlamını, çekme işlemini ve çekişin son sınıra ulaşması koşulunu korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Okçunun atıştan önce yayı mümkün olan en ileri çekiş noktasına getirdiği bağlamda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Yayın çekilmesini ve çekişin tam sınırına ulaşmasını birlikte korur.

branches.source_phrase_ar: أغرقت في القوس مددتها غاية المد (maqayis); أغرقت النبل وغرقته بلغت به غاية المد في القوس (ayn); أغرق النازع في القوس أي استوفى مدها (sihah); الإغراق في النزع أن ينزع حتى يشرب بالرصاف (tahdhib)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi tek bir yalın anlamdan çok, yapıya bağlı iki düzen kurar: atın sürüye karıştıktan sonra onu geçmesi ve bir şeyin alanı bütünüyle kaplaması ya da tüketmesi. Nefes, bakış ve koşum takımı örnekleri ikinci düzenin farklı katılımcılar üzerindeki gerçekleşmeleridir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: At yarışı kullanımında karışma ve ardından geçme birlikte gerekir; öteki kullanımlarda ortak sınır bir alanı veya kapasiteyi bütünüyle kapsamaktır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, at yarışı yapısını kapsama bildiren biçim ve söz öbeklerinden ayırır; hiçbir özel kullanım yalın kökün tek anlamı sayılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir kullanımda atın öteki atların arasına karışıp ardından hepsini geçmesi, başka kullanımlarda ise bir eylem veya nesnenin ilgili alanı ya da kapasiteyi bütünüyle kaplamasıdır. Nefesi sonuna kadar verme, bütün bakışları üzerinde toplama ve gövdenin koşum takımına sığmayacak ölçüde büyümesi bu ikinci düzenin özel gerçekleşmeleridir.

facets.statement: Bir alanın, sürenin veya kapasitenin hiçbir pay bırakmadan bütünüyle kapsanmasıdır.
At yarışında atın sürüye karışması ve bu karışmanın ardından öteki atları geçmesi iki aşamalı bir kullanımdır.
Nefes kullanımında soluk verme sürecinin bütün kapasitesi sonuna kadar kullanılır.
Bakış kullanımında bir kişi insanların dikkat alanını tümüyle kendisine bağlayıp başkasına pay bırakmaz.
Koşum kullanımında hayvanın yanları ve karnı, göğüs ve karın kayışlarının çevreleyebileceği alanı bütünüyle doldurur.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar atın öteki atlara karışıp sonra onları geçmesini ayrı bir yarış yapısı olarak verir. Kapsama düzeninde ise soluk verme bütünüyle sürdürülür, bir kişi bütün bakışları kendine çeker veya iri gövde koşum kayışlarının alanını doldurup onları dar bırakır.

concept_gloss.text: bir alanı tümüyle kapsama; sürüye karışıp öne geçme

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi süt veya başka bir içecekten alınan küçük miktarda birleşir. Miktarın kabın üçte biri, bir küçük kap dolusu, bundan daha azı veya bir içimlik olarak açıklanması kesin bir ölçü değil, küçük içecek payının kaynaklara göre değişen örnekleridir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal bir içeceğin küçük sunum miktarını anlatır; kabın tümü, susuzluğu gideren büyük içiş veya kapta kalan tortu zorunlu değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın adın küçük süt veya içecek payı anlamıyla sınırlıdır ve başka dallardaki boğulma ya da yumurta anlamlarını içeri almaz.

concept_map.definition: Sütten veya başka bir içecekten, bir içimlik ya da küçük bir kap dolusu sayılabilecek az miktardır. Kaynaklardaki üçte bir kap, bir küçük kap veya daha azı açıklamaları yaklaşık miktar çeşitleridir.

facets.statement: Süt veya başka bir içecekten içmeye ayrılmış küçük bir miktardır.
Miktar bir içimlik, küçük bir kap dolusu, bundan daha azı veya kabın yaklaşık üçte biri olarak değişik biçimlerde açıklanır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar sütü merkezde tutmakla birlikte başka içecekleri de kapsayan küçük bir içme payında birleşir. Verilen ölçüler bir içimlikten küçük bir kap dolusuna veya kabın yaklaşık üçte birine kadar değişir ve tek bir kesin hacim oluşturmaz.

concept_gloss.text: bir içimlik süt ya da başka içecek
concept_gloss.applicability: Sütü ve öteki içecekleri kapsayan küçük sunum miktarının en kısa doğal karşılığıdır.

error_profile.preserves: İçecek türünü, az miktarı ve tek seferde içilebilecek küçük pay niteliğini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Miktarın bir yudumdan fazla olabildiği, fakat yine de küçük bir sunum olarak kaldığı bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Kesin hacim dayatmadan içmeye ayrılan küçük miktar niteliğini korur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesindeki iki tanım aynı yumurta bölümünü açıkça göstermemektedir: biri yumurtanın iç kabuğunu, diğeri yenilen beyaz kısmı bildirir. Dal tek sözlüksel birim olarak korunabilir, ancak iki açıklamayı özdeşleştirmeden kaynak değişkeleri olarak sunmak gerekir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Karşılık, yumurtanın iç kabuğu ile yenilen beyaz kısmı arasında kaynaklara göre değişir; dış kabuk veya yumurtanın bütünü değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalnızca bu özel yumurta bölümü adına bağlıdır; biçimin kökün yalın anlamını temsil ettiği varsayılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Yumurtanın içinde bulunan ve bir açıklamada iç kabuk, başka bir açıklamada yenilen beyaz kısım olarak tanımlanan özel bir bölümdür. İki açıklama kaynak değişkeleri olarak korunur ve tek bir dokuymuş gibi birleştirilmez.

facets.statement: Bir açıklama söz konusu bölümü yumurtanın dış kabuğunun altında bulunan iç kabuk olarak tanımlar.
Başka bir açıklama söz konusu bölümü yumurtanın yenilen beyaz kısmı olarak tanımlar.
Sözcük biçiminin sonundaki ayırt edici sesin kökün asıl harflerinden olmadığı ayrıca belirtilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Sözlüksel birim yumurtanın içindeki bir bölümü adlandırır, ancak açıklamalar iç kabuk ile yenilen beyaz kısım arasında ayrılır. Biçimin sonundaki ayırt edici sesin köke ait olmadığına ilişkin bir dil bilgisi notu da bulunur.

error_profile.preserves: Yumurtanın bütününü değil, içte bulunan kabuk katmanını gösterir.

error_profile.preserves: Yumurtanın yenilen beyaz bölümünü diğer kabuk ve sarı bölümlerden ayırır.

neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal yumurtanın çatlayan kabuğunu ve buradan başka nesnelerin çatlayıp yarılmasını da kapsar.

neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal yumurtanın bütününü, kuş yumurtalarını ve yumurtlamayla ilgili adları kapsar.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal yalnızca gemi niteleyen söz öbeğinde, süsün veya gümüş bezemenin gemin tümüne yayılmasıyla sınırlıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım gemi niteleyen kalıba bağlıdır; genel süsleme, gümüş veya kaplama anlamı olarak yalınlaştırılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir gemin süslerle, özellikle gümüş bezemeyle, yüzeyi boyunca baştan başa kaplanmış olmasıdır. Tek bir süs parçası bulunması yeterli değildir; bezemenin geme yayılması gerekir.

facets.statement: Gem üzerindeki süsleme, yüzeyin bütününe yayılacak ölçüde kapsamlıdır.
Süslemenin gümüşle yapılması, kapsamlı bezemenin özellikle belirtilen bir gerçekleşmesidir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar belirli bir gemin süsle kaplanmasında birleşir; gümüş bezeme açıkça verilen özel malzemedir. Niteleme, süsün tek noktada bulunmasından çok gemin bütününe yayılmasını anlatır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Yalnızca süslemenin gemin bütününe yayıldığı, gümüşün de kullanılabildiği niteleme için geçerlidir.

error_profile.preserves: Gem nesnesini, süslemeyi ve bezemenin yüzey boyunca bütünüyle yayılması koşulunu korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Gemin bezemesinde kullanılan malzemenin özellikle gümüş olduğu bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Gemi, gümüş bezeme ve bezemenin geniş yüzeye yayılması özelliklerini korur.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: baştan başa süslenmiş veya gümüşle kaplanmış gem

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dalı gem nesnesine ve süslemenin gemin bütününe yayılması koşuluna bağlıdır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal takı, silah süsü ve kişinin süs takması gibi genel bezeme alanlarını kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da bir nesneyi değerli veya gösterişli bezeklerle donatma alanını paylaşır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu dal süs nesnesini ve süslenmeyi genel olarak adlandırır; odak dalıysa yalnızca baştan başa bezeli gemi niteleyen yapıdır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dalı gümüşün de kullanılabildiği kapsamlı bir gem süslemesi durumudur.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal gümüş maddesini ve gümüşten yapılmış ya da gümüş kakılmış nesneleri adlandırır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Gümüş, odak daldaki gem bezemesinin kullanılabilen özel malzemesidir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu dal malzemeyi adlandırır; odak dalı malzeme gümüş olsun veya olmasın süslemenin belirli bir nesneyi bütünüyle kaplaması durumunu anlatır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; genel süs dalı yapı ve kapsam sınırını, gümüş dalıysa nesne ile malzeme ayrımını en iyi gösterdi. Öteki eyer, örtü ve süs parçaları yalnızca aynı donatım alanında kaldı.
